summary: isalpha checks whether a string is nonempty and every character is classified as an alphabetic letter by Python’s Unicode rules.
documentation: isalpha checks whether a string is nonempty and every character is classified as an alphabetic letter by Python’s Unicode rules. It accepts letters beyond ASCII but rejects spaces, digits and punctuation.
returns: True for a nonempty letter-only string, otherwise False.
caution: Human names often contain spaces, apostrophes and hyphens, so this is not a suitable general name validator. Decomposed combining marks can also make the result false.
scenarios: Classify letter-only tokens in an import preview.
Separate alphabetic prefixes from numeric or punctuated labels.
Teach the difference between Unicode letters and ASCII-only checks.
title: Classify letter-only tokens
problem: Return whether input is a nonempty string containing only Unicode letters according to str.isalpha. Do not trim, normalize or remove punctuation.
hint: Apply isalpha directly to the original string.
goal: Use str.isalpha() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
